items.title: OpenAI closes first $11bn of new round at $1.25tn valuation, below its $30bn target
items.summary: Reuters, citing a source, reported that OpenAI closed an initial $11bn of a new round at a $1.25tn valuation, with SoftBank and MGX reportedly taking part. Bloomberg reported the round could reach about $20bn in the coming weeks. OpenAI had reportedly sought up to $30bn at $1.4-1.5tn. Figures rest on anonymous sources.
items.why_it_matters: A round well below target suggests investor appetite for the highest AI valuations is cooling.

items.title: Nvidia board opens independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese intelligence link
items.summary: Nvidia's board formed an independent committee, with outside counsel, to review reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The reports centre on Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer that reportedly bought $4.8bn of Nvidia chips. Huang has confirmed a personal relationship with her and remains CEO. The intelligence and chip-diversion claims are unconfirmed, and China calls them groundless. Three House committee chairs reportedly asked for a closed-door briefing on Nov 18.
items.why_it_matters: Governance and export-control risk at the world's most valuable AI chip company arrives just before its earnings report.

items.title: AI stocks rebound after a $2.5tn sell-off, with rate and midterm worries behind the volatility
items.summary: AI-linked stocks lost about $2.5tn from the Nasdaq 100 on Nov 5, pushing the Nasdaq Composite into correction territory. Shares then rebounded. On Nov 11, AP reported the S&P 500 up about 1% and the Nasdaq up 1.6%. Micron rose 11.7%, Broadcom 5.3% and Nvidia 3.2%. A worse-than-expected inflation report raised expectations of Fed rate hikes, and investors worry that Democratic gains could bring limits on data-centre construction.
items.why_it_matters: Higher borrowing costs and possible data-centre restrictions are now tied to how AI is valued in the market.

items.title: CoreWeave beats Q3 estimates and raises 2026 outlook; shares jump about 22%
items.summary: CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue of $3.66bn, up 168% year on year, and raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0-13.3bn. Backlog $132.5bn, net loss $709m. Capex guidance $37-39bn. The stock rose about 22% on Nov 11.
items.why_it_matters: A direct read on demand for AI compute, and on how heavy the debt and capex load is for AI infrastructure firms.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab reportedly raising about $5bn at a $40bn pre-money valuation, led by Accel
items.summary: Business Insider, as relayed by Tech Funding News, reports Thinking Machines Lab is raising about $5bn at $40bn pre-money. Accel is the only named participant. Reported, not confirmed.
items.why_it_matters: One of the largest AI seed-stage cheques ever, at a valuation lower than previously discussed.
